title: Penalty shoot-outs are a lottery, so stop pretending otherwise

defects.quote: The penalty spot is ten yards from goal
defects.correction: The penalty mark is 12 yards (11 metres) from the goal line.

defects.quote: The World Cup's first shoot-out came in the 1982 semi-final, when Italy beat France in Seville
defects.correction: The first World Cup shoot-out was West Germany's win over France in the 1982 semi-final in Seville.
defects.note: [multi-part] The round, the year, the losing side and the city are right; only the winning team is wrong.

defects.quote: Left-footed takers miss twice as often as right-footed ones in shoot-outs.
Shoot-outs are pure luck, so practising them is a waste of training time.
defects.known_rebuttal: Shoot-out outcomes are not random. Research on penalty-taking finds that technique, routine and how long a player takes after the whistle all affect conversion, and goalkeepers who study takers' habits save more. Germany have won nearly all of their major-tournament shoot-outs, and England, after years of defeats, won their first World Cup shoot-out in 2018 following deliberate preparation; a pure lottery would not produce such persistent differences or respond to practice.

defects.quote: All warfare is based on deception.
defects.source_title: The Art of War by Sun Tzu, translated by Lionel Giles
